narrative:
The model estimates a 55% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your total professional experience stands out as the strongest influence pushing the model toward predicting you will leave. With over 11 years across your career, you have significantly more experience than most employees the model expects to stay—only 14.7% of those predicted to stay have this level of seniority. The model sees this as a sign that you may be ready for new opportunities elsewhere.

Your time with the current organization (1-5 years) is the second most important factor and also pulls the prediction toward leaving. This relatively short tenure in your present role, compared to longer stays among those expected to remain, suggests you have not yet built the deep roots that typically encourage retention.

Interestingly, the fact that you have not received other job offers while working here works in your favor and is the third most influential element. It nudges the prediction slightly back toward staying, as most employees the model expects to remain also report no external opportunities.

The organization should consider discussing your long-term career goals with you and exploring ways to increase your sense of belonging in your current role. You may want to reflect on whether your extensive experience aligns with your future aspirations here or elsewhere.
